meetings.headline: The budget lands in the black, and the school year is in full swing
meetings.record_note: These notes were made with AI assistance from a single room microphone, and the recording quality was poor in places. Every number below was checked against the recording and cross-checked with the district's published agenda, and where the audio was not clear enough to be sure of something, we left it out rather than guess. The official district minutes remain the authoritative record. Corrections are always welcome and get fixed promptly.

items.title: The budget ends the year $194,000 in the black
items.why: The June budget had projected just $3,143. Property taxes came in 12.9 percent over what was budgeted, helped by a $126,000 transportation reimbursement and a $181,000 grant. The fund balance is projected to rise from $479,000 to $673,000, moving toward the district's $1 million long-term goal. The board also approved building a committed reserve of 3 percent of expenses (about $200,000 to $220,000): the fund already holds $45,000, with $125,000 set aside this year and $50,000 next year. Passed by voice vote. The first interim budget comes in December.

items.title: Every family took part in the Shark fundraiser
items.why: At $40,000 raised against a $50,000 goal with two days to go, participation reached every family in the school. Ahead: a pancake breakfast with Santa, a tamale dinner at the winter festival, and a winter concert with Big Buddies and Little Buddies singing together, followed by cider and a luminary walk. Shark is funding the music teacher preparing the concert, music training for teachers, and a monthly wellness activity for staff, and a local author will visit each grade during reading week.

items.title: A USDA grant of about $57,000 brings a garden aide
items.why: The grant to the food service program funds a garden aide, freeing Hunter to return to the kitchen. The job posting is up. The garden program also grows produce for student lunches, the same farm-to-table work Measure M will now support for the next four years.

items.title: Enrollment holds at 207, with two new team members
items.why: Tammy started part time on November 2, and Jeanette started November 3 as a full-time special education aide.

items.title: Conflict-of-interest code updated for the first time since 2001
items.why: Resolution 2627, requested by the county, modernizes the list of positions that file annual disclosures: the board, the superintendent/principal, and the chief business official. Passed by voice vote.

items.title: Developer fee set at $3.72 per square foot
items.why: The residential fee rises from $3.31, effective January, following the state study, and is shared with the high school district. The annual report showed five payments last year, deposited in Fund 25, which is reserved for construction. A motion to approve the fee was made; the recording did not capture a second or a vote call.

items.title: Bond project list approved; campus work moves ahead
items.why: The board gave conceptual approval to the project list, which allows the district to request architect qualifications without committing to any project. The district's side of the PG&E work is done; PG&E has been sent an appeal letter after missing its January window. New storage units are being built, and property-line fencing was walked with the committee.

items.title: Grounds and forest stewardship
items.why: Crews are clearing brush and tan oak lost to sudden oak death, with a controlled burn planned for spring. A trail is being scouted on the district's southwest parcel along the old rail line. The eroding creek bank near the parking lot was inspected by a geotechnical engineer, with a likely boulder repair in permitting.

items.title: Regional planning for special education
items.why: The West County Consortium, which pools special education classes and staff among the small West County districts, will see a change of host as the high school district steps back after 15 to 20 years. The county office has brought in a consultant to guide the transition. Harmony's planned bond build-out includes five classrooms, with space for a special day class.

items.title: An administrative restructure takes shape for next year
items.why: This year, county office support is covering business duties, shared among Melina, Lindsay, and Stephanie. Next year's plan would combine the superintendent and chief business official roles and promote the assistant principal to principal, saving about $127,000. The board asked to hear from staff first and to see the roles clearly defined before anything is decided; a detailed plan returns at the next meeting.

items.title: Support steps for staff
items.why: Following this year's reductions, the board and superintendent outlined steps for the months ahead: board listening sessions with staff two or three times a year, one-on-one conversations available with union representation if staff prefer, and a master's project by staff member Micah to pilot short relief breaks during the day.

items.title: Looking ahead
items.why: Stacey, the business manager, stays through December before starting a new role, with thanks for her years of service. Two new board members will be onboarded before the next meeting on December 15, when the first interim budget also arrives.

items.title: Facilities master plan adopted; state application authorized
items.why: Three unanimous OPSC items: correcting the district's 2012 filing, submitting the 2026 one, and adopting Resolution 20261030 — the facilities master plan plus authorization to apply to the state's school-construction funding program. This is the pipeline the board has been assembling since September's $17M needs list, now formalized as a state application. In and out in an hour (8:57–10:01 AM), every vote unanimous.

items.title: Two hires approved
items.why: A special-education paraeducator and a custodial/maintenance technician — the October starts flagged at the September meeting.

items.title: November meeting moved
items.why: November 12 shifts to Monday, November 16, 2026 — 7:00 PM via Google Meet per the district calendar.

items.title: Pathways financials on the November agenda
items.why: The board requested a November discussion item: a Pathways financial explanation and how it affects Harmony Union School District.

meetings.headline: The first real bond money moves

items.title: Bond contracts approved — about $83K
items.why: Unanimous consent (Laird/Solter): cargo storage ($34,000), EOC pad ($13,000), perimeter survey ($8,000), septic risers ($12,000), and cistern/garden water overflow ($16,000) — the first Measure M bond contracts actually executed, not just budgeted.

items.title: Field trips (consent)
items.why: Overnight and water-related student trips approved.

items.title: William's Law quarterly reports
items.why: Q4 2025-26 and Q1 2026-27 school-safety reporting approved unanimously — the state's quarterly confirmation the district is current.

items.title: Five minutes flat
items.why: The open session ran 9:16 to 9:21 PM — every vote unanimous, no discussion on the record. The board's real work that night happened in closed session beforehand; the open session was the rapid-fire sign-off.

items.title: Next meeting: November 12
items.why: Confirmed on the record — since moved to November 16 per the October 30 minutes.

items.title: 2025-26 unaudited actuals approved — unanimous
items.why: Convened 8:49 AM, adjourned 8:52 AM — the meeting's one substantive act. The district's closed books for 2025-26 (Gress/Laird, unanimous), headed to the county office. The full report runs about a hundred pages; the headline numbers are on the budget page — including an attendance shortfall worth roughly $160K in state funding.

meetings.headline: The workhorse — nine approvals, every vote unanimous

items.title: Money items
items.why: LCAP revisions, unaudited actuals, the Gann limit (the state's spending cap), and substitute teacher compensation — all approved unanimously.

items.title: Facilities and energy
items.why: PCO Energy Resiliency Project, a PG&E contract, and a new facilities fee schedule — all approved.

items.title: New math pilot
items.why: Innovamat Thinking Math approved for piloting.

items.title: The bond pipeline
items.why: $17M in identified project needs; $1M–$2.5M potentially bond-fundable; committee phases finalized, due January 2027.

items.title: People
items.why: New special-education and custodial hires start in October. Closed session covered union negotiations (CSEA and HUTA), anticipated litigation, and the superintendent's review.

items.title: shARK fundraising
items.why: $11K pledged toward a $20K goal.

items.title: What's coming
items.why: Parcel tax discussions (Koslen), a Town Hall on October 15, and new-board-member training January 14.

items.title: Closed session: two anticipated litigation matters
items.why: Almost the entire hour was legal counsel in closed session. No report out, no votes, no dollars. The public record is essentially "we met with our lawyer."
